sentences.text:
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of the the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.247 of 2023 at Police Station-Bhitauli District-Maharajganj under Section 376, 452 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of of POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(5) of SC/ST Act.
The applicant is in jail since 22.10.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by trial court on 16.11.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Parmeshwar Yadav, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Chandan Agrawal, learned AGA from the Ajmat vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105980559/
1 record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The F.I.R. arises out of a dispute between the parties over a theft of mobile phone.
2. The applicant was implicated to only to settle the dispute on terms of the victim's family.
3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The victim in her testimony before the trial court has also repudiated the prosecution case.
She has not identified the applicant as the principal offender who committed rape with her.
The victim has been declared hostile at the instance of the prosecution.

4. Similarly, the father of the victim who is the first informant too has refuted the prosecution case in his deposition before the trial court and has been declared hostile at the instance of the prosecution.
5. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
6. The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated with the police investigations and had joined the trial.
7. The applicant never influenced any witness or tampered with the evidence.
8. The applicant never adopted any dilatory tactics or impeded the process of the trial.
9. The trial is moving at a snail's pace and is not likely to conclude anytime in the near future.
The applicant is not responsible for the delay in the trial.

10. Inordinate delay in concluding trial had has led to virtually an indefinite imprisonment of the applicant without there being any credible evidence to implicate him in the offence and violates the rights of the applicant to speedy trial.
11. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
12. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Ajmat vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105980559/

sentences.text: Let the applicant-Ajmat be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii )
The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
Order Date :- 16.4.2024 Dhananjai  Ajmat vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105980559/
